page.reads: The right-side companion to the method engine. The method engine breaks a text into moves and wires them; THIS engine renders that finalized output into figures for two audiences, composing into a reading room. Each visual is a node with a spec-drawer (what it shows, which method node + feed it reads, its encoding, its four-check gate). The grammar every node obeys, and the gate every node passes, live on the design principles page. Validated by 3DR-16.

seam: This engine's INPUT is the method's FINALIZED feeds (Text=checkout.json · Decompose=moves.json · Connect=connect_node_drawer.json); the TRANSFORMATION is design-SB's. A node reads_from a feed field — it never re-authors a method fact (that was the Connect-status bug). Un-finalized engines (Situate / Frame / Gloss) are out of scope until finalized.

contract.title: The SSOT render contract — how these pages stay honest
contract.intro: Content-owner SBs (Method · Atlas Reader · Librarian) update their OWN SSOT engine pages; Design SB owns the render contract + a periodic review, not every change. This kills the bottleneck (no single Design session gates every edit) and the lost handoff (transcription that rots in chat).

tiers: Top of each Design session (~10 min): quick sweep for drift + fresh hardcoding.
Sprint boundary / when handoffs land: the deeper pass.
checks: Does it still make sense? — numbers agree, copy matches the data, no orphaned refs, drawers render (human judgment).
Is anything hardcoded that shouldn't be? — pre-screened by a mechanical ssot_hardcode_scan (TBD-build), human-confirmed → §2.16 defect → converted.

rules: You make your own update — don't hand Design a blob to transcribe.
Heads-up to Design on major changes.
const P edits: parse → modify → serialize, never string-subs.
Cache-bust rendered assets when you change them.
Done = rendered + verified live, not data-on-main.
The page is the authority; markdown is subordinate.
Provenance + methodology footer on every feed/script/doc.
Track handoffs in the registry/DWS, not chat.
